rows.evidence: unvalidated addFixedDay inflates the reward counter so claimDDDD mints/claims oversized DDDD rewards.

rows.name: ArbitrumBaseSwapper
rows.evidence: public swapTokensForExactTokens spends the contract's own token balance and refunds the remainder to a caller-controlled recipient.

rows.name: BaseBebopSettlement
rows.evidence: Bebop settle() executed caller-supplied interaction transferFrom calldata against accounts that had approved the settlement contract, with no maker-signature/auth check.

rows.name: Bebop_dex
rows.evidence: Same Bebop/Jam settle() flaw: empty-signature order with attacker-supplied interactions ran transferFrom against victims' standing allowances.

rows.name: BeefyZapRouter
rows.evidence: BeefyZapRouter.executeOrder ran arbitrary route steps (transferFrom of vault tokens) only gated by msg.sender==order.user, letting attacker spend third-party allowances.

rows.name: EquilibriaEPendle
rows.evidence: VaultEPendle did not update reward debt on share transfers and public getReward(account) let fresh receivers re-claim the same native rewards repeatedly.

rows.name: EverValueCoin
rows.evidence: EVA orderbook addNewOrder logic let a flashloan-funded caller obtain EVA that was dumped for WBTC on Uniswap, an accounting flaw in the order entrypoint.

rows.name: Grizzifi
rows.evidence: _incrementUplineTeamCount used totalInvested (including withdrawn) instead of active investments, letting chained accounts farm referral/milestone bonuses.

rows.name: MulticallWithXera
rows.evidence: Xera token's _msgSender() trusted the Multicall forwarder, so aggregate3 transferFrom spoofed the victim as sender and spent its approval to Multicall.

rows.name: PendleReflector
rows.evidence: Reflector.reflect trusted caller-supplied Pendle market/limit-router calldata while operating on its own token balances, letting a fake limit router pull the Pendle router's balance.

rows.name: SizeCredit
rows.evidence: leverageUpWithSwap did not validate the GenericRoute swap data, allowing an arbitrary transferFrom(victim,...) call using the victim's allowance.

rows.name: YuliAI
rows.evidence: Victim contract priced YULIAI sells off the YULIAI/USDT V3 pool spot price, which the attacker moved with a flashloan before selling into the victim.

rows.name: unverified_6f7a
rows.evidence: Proxy selector 0xbfd479c4 processed arbitrary token amounts with no caller authorization or ownership check, letting anyone route the victim's live balances into a liquidity path.

rows.name: unverified_d132
rows.evidence: Victim swapSingleToken trusted an attacker-supplied fake pair and paid DAI in the swap callback without authenticating a real pool.

rows.name: NGP
rows.evidence: NGP token's _update() had a sync() bug that reduced the pair's NGP reserve during transfers, letting a flashloan swap capture the manipulated price.

rows.name: MIMSpell3
rows.evidence: Abracadabra cauldron cook() REPAY action accounting flaw let the attacker withdraw MIM from BentoBox across cauldrons without real repayment.

rows.name: DRLVaultV3
rows.evidence: DRLVault.swapToWETH traded through the USDC/WETH pool with no effective slippage guard, so the attacker sandwiched the vault after manipulating the pool price.

rows.name: yETH
rows.evidence: yETH stableswap pool add/remove_liquidity and permissionless update_rates math could be driven (with OETH rebase) to skew vb_prod/sum and drain the pool.

rows.name: LAXO_Token
rows.evidence: LAXO token's transfer/liquidity mechanics let the attacker collapse the busd_pair LAXO reserve and swap out inflated USDT, a flaw in the token's pair-balance handling.

rows.name: Moonwell
rows.evidence: Moonwell's cbETH Chainlink oracle reported a faulty cbETH price, letting the attacker liquidate a borrow and arbitrage the difference against Aerodrome's real price.

rows.name: ATMBlindBox
rows.evidence: After blockhash(betBlock+2) expired, settlement fell back to keccak256(prevrandao,betId,timestamp), predictable randomness the attacker could evaluate before settling a winning bet.

rows.name: Univ3CollateralToken
rows.evidence: Univ3CollateralToken valued deposited Uni V3 positions per minter rather than per vault, so one NFT counted as collateral for all 30 of the minter's vaults.

rows.name: WhalebitOracleManipulation
rows.evidence: Whalebit priced staking levels off the CES/USDT Algebra pool spot price, which the attacker moved with flashloaned CES to withdraw more than deposited.

rows.name: unverified_1304
rows.evidence: An old CheckoutPool bridge operator had _ALLOW_ALL_ enabled and no operator gate on bridge(), so any caller could drive the paymaster/pool to pay a checkout's target amount from pool excess.

rows.name: JUDAO
rows.evidence: JUDAO's sell transfer hook (sync mining + isBurnPair reserve burns) credited excess JUDAO to the pair, which the attacker then swapped out for USDT.

rows.name: PerpPair
rows.evidence: Attacker acted as both LP and trader: an oversized long skewed PerpPair's virtual AMM and the LP immediately realized inflated PnL, a mechanism-design flaw with no code defect or external oracle.

rows.name: RWAVault
rows.evidence: RWAVault overrode ERC4626 withdraw() without the allowance spend when msg.sender!=owner, letting the attacker withdraw eight depositors' balances.

rows.name: SingularityDynaVault
rows.evidence: dynBaseUSDCv3 oracle path (Uni V3 fee tier 42 / zero-liquidity fallbacks) made totalAssets() count only idle USDC, so a flashloan deposit minted inflated shares redeemable for the real reserves.

rows.name: giddyvaultv3_compound_auth
rows.evidence: GiddyVaultV3 EIP-712 compound auth covered only keccak256(SwapInfo.data), so the attacker reused a valid signature with attacker-controlled fromToken/toToken/amount/aggregator to drain strategies.

rows.name: unverified_a152
rows.evidence: An authorized spender's helper spendFromUser let the spender pull any user's tokens via the shared AllowanceTarget approvals, an access-control flaw draining approved balances.

rows.name: AROS
rows.evidence: AROS claimPrincipal/claimYield reward logic let a flashloan-funded position (acquired via Venus/Aave/Balancer/V3 flashes) claim principal and yield far exceeding real entitlement, then dump AROS.

rows.name: AdsharesBridge
rows.evidence: The privileged bridge minter minted wADS to the attacker with fabricated native from/txid values, i.e. the mint authority was used to fake cross-chain deposits.

rows.name: DxSale
rows.evidence: Deployer laundered locker ownership through 89 wallets, then the final owner used the owner-only DXLOCKERLP() backdoor to drain all locked LP positions past their timelocks.

rows.name: Ekubo
rows.evidence: Ekubo's lock/forward/withdraw/pay flow let an attacker withdraw core-held WBTC and settle the debt via pay() using the victim's approval, abusing the router's flawed settlement.

rows.name: ElevateFi
rows.evidence: ElevateFi getPriceUSD read raw DAI/EFI pair reserves, so the attacker pumped the pair spot price to create underpriced package-7 stakes and claim inflated EFI rewards.

rows.name: FractalProtocol
rows.evidence: Fractal vault deposit/compute/withdraw share-price accounting was manipulable within one tx by a flashloaned deposit, letting the attacker withdraw more USDC.e than deposited.

rows.name: HumaCreditApprovalBypass
rows.evidence: requestCredit()+refreshAccount() flipped an un-approved credit line to GoodStanding without EA approval, letting an attacker drawdown each pool's full liquidity.

rows.name: INKFinance
rows.evidence: INK payroll claimPayroll scaled the payout to the instantaneous treasury balance, so seeding the treasury with a flashloan before claiming drained excess USDT.

rows.name: JoeAgent
rows.evidence: removeLiquidityViaContract forwarded BNB before zeroing lpInfo (CEI violation), letting the attacker re-enter and withdraw one LP position ~25x.

rows.name: LegendaryMoneyMonNft
rows.evidence: cliamRewred's recoverSigner never rejected ecrecover's address(0) return, and admin was set to zero, so a (r=0,s=0,v=27) signature passed verify() and drained the MON balance.

rows.name: MAPProtocol
rows.evidence: MAP OmniService retryMessageIn accepted a crafted message payload without valid cross-chain proof verification, minting 1e15 MAPO to the attacker.

rows.name: NewMarketTrading
rows.evidence: SquidRouterModule's Axelar express path did gateway-less execution and never checked msg.sender==delegate, so a forged payload drove the victim Safe to swap its USDC into an attacker pool.

rows.name: Renegade
rows.evidence: Renegade dark-pool proxy's initialize was unprotected, letting the attacker set attacker-controlled injectedLogic that updateWallet delegatecalled to drain 26 tokens.

rows.name: SEAToken
rows.evidence: MetaSea Round open/redeemPosition accounting paid out SEA from the distributor exceeding the deposit, drained in a 12x flashloan loop.

rows.name: SKP
rows.evidence: The SKP owner used the owner-only ownerBurnLiquidityPairTokens backdoor to burn LP-held SKP and sync, inflating the price to over-borrow BTCB/USDT as collateral.

rows.name: SQTokenStaking
rows.evidence: SQTokenStaking transferOwnership had no access control, so the attacker seized ownership and used owner functions (stakeOwner/withdrawalTokens) to drain SQi.

rows.name: SharwaMarginTrading
rows.evidence: Sharwa valued Hegic option NFT collateral via a Uniswap V3 spot Quoter path, which the attacker skewed (USDC/USDC.e) in the ERC721 callback to over-borrow.

rows.name: TesseraSwap
rows.evidence: TesseraSwap sent out USDC before collecting the owed WETH in the callback with amountCheck=0, so the attacker bought the WETH cheaper and kept the spread.

rows.name: TrustedVolumes
rows.evidence: RFQ proxy had permissionless registerAllowedOrderSigner and checked authorization against order.taker (attacker) instead of order.maker, draining the maker's approved balances.

rows.name: VerusBridge
rows.evidence: Verus submitImports accepted a crafted partialtransactionproof/MMR proof that bypassed VerusProof validation, minting fake ETH/tBTC/USDC imports.

rows.name: AISOTHPresale
rows.evidence: AISOTH presale sold its full AIS inventory at a fixed price below AMM market with no limits, so a flashloan buy-claim-dump arbitrage extracted USDT.

rows.name: BOSS
rows.evidence: BOSS token/helper mint/burn mechanics let the attacker collapse the pair's BOSS reserve to dust and repeatedly swap out USDT, a flaw in the token's supply/burn handling.

rows.name: CookFinanceIssuance
rows.evidence: issueWithSingleToken2 accepted attacker-supplied component weightings and traded CKToken holdings via a Pancake spot adapter with zero minimum output, turning a 1-unit issue into real outflows.

rows.name: DIP
rows.evidence: DIP's sell-fee plus a double router-transfer bug let the attacker use skim/sync to shrink the pair's DIP reserve and swap out nearly all pair AIC.

rows.name: DLMC
rows.evidence: DLMCToken buy/sell used a reserve-derived livePrice; the attacker inflated it with buys then sold at the inflated price to drain the contract's USDT.

rows.name: DTXT
rows.evidence: A 1-wei USDT transfer made DTXT misclassify a large pair transfer as liquidity addition, bypassing sell fees before swapping DTXT out for USDT.

rows.name: JB
rows.evidence: JB's gateway cycle used the live JB balance to sell/burn/sync through the JB/USDT pair, releasing pair USDT via flawed token/reward mechanics.

rows.name: LixirPermitDrain
rows.evidence: Lixir vault-token permit accepted a dummy signature as long as ecrecover returned any nonzero address, so a forged permit granted allowance to drain every holder's shares.

rows.name: OLPC
rows.evidence: OLPC's decimalsValue-scaled transfer/burn hook let dust transfers plus sync/skim decay the pair's OLPC reserve, so a zero-input supporting-fee swap released LABUBU.

rows.name: RoyalRoyalties
rows.evidence: Royal1155LDA incremented per-tier balance bookkeeping even for zero-amount batch items, inflating tierBalanceOf to 100 vs supply 1 so Royalties paid a 100x claim.

rows.name: ThetanutsFi
rows.evidence: After claim() crushed totalSupply to 3 wei, mint()'s deposit = basket*amount/totalSupply truncated to 0, letting the attacker mint shares for free and keep the basket.

rows.name: Thetanuts
rows.evidence: Same Thetanuts index-vault flaw: flash-borrow shares, claim to crush totalSupply, then free-mint via integer-division truncation to repay and keep component vaults.

rows.name: WHALE
rows.evidence: WHALE's transfer pipeline (LP credit staging, POL flush, hashrate settlement) let the attacker create a pair reserve imbalance and swap out USDT, a token-accounting flaw.

rows.name: SummerFi
rows.evidence: FleetCommander NAV summed each Ark's totalAssets() with no manipulation guard, so donating cheap vgUSDC into an empty ark inflated share value and the attacker redeemed to drain other LPs.

rows.name: edel-xstock
rows.evidence: Edel lending market valued wrapped xStock collateral via a mutable ERC4626 convertToAssets() rate, so donating underlying GOOGLx inflated collateral value in-tx to over-borrow reserves.
